mainTopic: Placement of the נר חנוכה, the ban on treating מצוה objects with contempt (חנוכה light, נויי סוכה, כיסוי הדם), and רב and שמואל on lighting from lamp to lamp
overview: This amud finishes the rules for placing the נר חנוכה. Above twenty אמות it is invalid, like a סוכה and a מבוי. It should go within a טפח of the doorway, on the left side, opposite the מזוזה. The same teachers also give a short אגדה about יוסף's pit: it had no water, but it had snakes and scorpions. רב forbids counting money by the חנוכה light. רב יוסף explains that the reason is not holiness but avoiding contempt for מצוות, learned from כיסוי הדם, which must be done by hand and not by foot. רב יוסף then rejects using the חנוכה rule to prove the ban on using נויי סוכה, which a ברייתא already teaches, and calls blood the source of them all. Next, רב and שמואל disagree on three matters: lighting from one חנוכה lamp to another, moving ציצית between garments, and dragging furniture on שבת like רבי שמעון. אביי reports that רבה followed שמואל in all three. Two reasons are offered for רב's ban on lighting from lamp to lamp, ביזוי מצוה and אכחושי מצוה, and the גמרא shows how they differ in practice. רב אויא then begins an objection that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A נר חנוכה placed above twenty אמות is invalid
steps.stepSummary: A נר חנוכה placed higher than twenty אמות does not count, just like a סוכה or a מבוי that is too tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נר חנוכה that someone placed higher than twenty אמות is invalid, just like a סוכה and just like a מבוי that are too high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: a נר חנוכה placed above twenty אמות is invalid. It compares this to two other cases with the same height limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do not normally look up above twenty אמות. The whole point of the נר חנוכה is to be seen (פרסומי ניסא), so a lamp placed that high fails its purpose. The same logic invalidates a סוכה roof and a מבוי crossbeam above that height, because they also need to be noticed.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway, which needs a crossbeam to permit carrying on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the upper height limit for lighting נר חנוכה in practical halacha.

phrases.english: A Hanukkah lamp that one placed
above twenty cubits is invalid,
like a sukka and like an alleyway.
phrases.notes: Both are invalid above twenty cubits because the eye does not notice things that high.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵר שֶׁל חֲנוּכָּה שֶׁהִנִּיחָה לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings that רב כהנא quoted in the name of רב נתן בר מניומי, which began on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נר חנוכה placed above twenty אמות is invalid, like a סוכה and a מבוי.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק about יוסף's pit say 'no water'?
steps.stepSummary: Using the same chain of teachers, the גמרא asks why the פסוק adds 'there was no water in it' after already saying the pit was empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב כהנא said that רב נתן בר מניומי taught in the name of רב תנחום: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'and the pit was empty, there was no water in it'? From the fact that it says 'the pit was empty,' don't I already know there was no water in it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another teaching from the same teachers, this one about יוסף's pit. It asks why the פסוק repeats itself, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Empty' already tells us there was no water, so the extra words look unnecessary. The question assumes that the תורה does not waste words. Every extra phrase must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

steps.confusionAlert: This teaching has nothing to do with חנוכה. It appears here only because it was taught by the same chain of teachers (רב כהנא, רב נתן בר מניומי, רב תנחום).

phrases.english: And Rav Kahana said,
Rav Natan bar Manyumi expounded
in the name of Rav Tanchum:
What is that which is written:
'And the pit was empty, there was no water in it'?
phrases.notes: בראשית ל״ז:כ״ד, about יוסף's brothers throwing him into the pit.

phrases.english: From the implication of what is said, 'and the pit was empty,'
don't I know that there was no water in it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching from the same transmitters, even though the topic is unrelated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the seemingly extra words 'there was no water in it' come to teach.

steps.title: No water, but snakes and scorpions
steps.stepSummary: The extra words teach that the pit had no water, but it did have snakes and scorpions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, why does the verse say 'there was no water in it'? To teach that water was not in it, but snakes and scorpions were in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The extra phrase limits what was missing: only water was missing, and dangerous creatures were there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words are read as a limiting phrase: 'water there was none,' which implies something else was there. This shows that יוסף was thrown into real danger. It deepens the account of what the brothers did.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the verse come to teach (by these extra words)?

phrases.english: Rather, why does the verse say
'there was no water in it'?
Water there was none in it,
but snakes and scorpions there were in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the extra words in the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pit lacked only water; it contained snakes and scorpions.

steps.title: The lamp belongs within a handbreadth of the doorway
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that the מצוה is to place the נר חנוכה within the טפח closest to the doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is a מצוה to place the נר חנוכה within the טפח next to the entrance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the laws of חנוכה. רבה says exactly where the lamp should go: right next to the doorway, within one טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beyond the height limit, there is also a rule for how far the lamp may be from the doorway. Placing it close to the entrance shows that it belongs to this house's מצוה. The word מצוה signals that this is the ideal way to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה (the ideal way) to place it

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The Hanukkah lamp: it is a מצוה to place it
within the handbreadth adjacent to the entrance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the אגדה to the placement laws of נר חנוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נר חנוכה should ideally be placed within a טפח of the doorway.

steps.title: On which side of the doorway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the lamp goes on the right or the left side of the doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where does he place it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short clarifying question about רבה's rule. It sets up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doorway has two sides, and רבה did not say which one. The question asks for this missing detail.

keyTerms.meaning: And where does he place it?

phrases.english: And where does he place it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a detail missing from רבה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the lamp goes on the right or the left side of the doorway.

steps.title: Right side or left side: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא says the right side; רב שמואל מדפתי says the left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said: On the right. רב שמואל from Difti said: On the left.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question differently. One says right, and one says left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right side is usually given preference in halacha, which explains the first opinion. The reason for the left side is given in the next step, when the גמרא decides the halacha.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר: מִיָּמִין
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said: On the right.
Rav Shmuel from Difti said:
On the left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two answers to the question of which side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a dispute: right side (רב אחא בריה דרבא) or left side (רב שמואל מדפתי).

steps.title: The halacha: lamp on the left, מזוזה on the right
steps.stepSummary: The halacha follows the left-side view, so that the נר חנוכה and the מזוזה are on opposite sides of the doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the halacha is: on the left, so that the נר חנוכה will be on the left and the מזוזה on the right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the dispute in favor of the left side and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזוזה is already on the right side. Putting the lamp on the left means that a person walking in is surrounded by מצוות on both sides. This explains why the left side wins here even though the right is usually preferred.

keyTerms.meaning: The scroll fixed to the right doorpost

steps.whatToRemember: The נר חנוכה goes within a טפח of the doorway, on the left side, opposite the מזוזה on the right.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the accepted practical halacha for where to place the חנוכה lights at a doorway.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: on the left,
so that the Hanukkah lamp will be on the left
and the mezuza on the right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute from the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The lamp is placed on the left, so that one is surrounded by מצוות: the מזוזה on the right and the נר חנוכה on the left.

steps.title: Do not count money by the נר חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that one may not count money by the light of the נר חנוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רב אסי said that רב said: It is forbidden to count money opposite a נר חנוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new law is introduced: the light of the נר חנוכה may not be used for personal tasks like counting coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting money is a weekday, practical use of the light. רב forbids even this kind of benefit from the מצוה light. The reason behind the rule is debated in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Asi said that Rav said:
It is forbidden to count money
opposite a Hanukkah light.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic within the laws of נר חנוכה: benefiting from its light.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to use the light of the נר חנוכה for personal tasks such as counting money.

steps.title: שמואל asks: Is the lamp holy?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל challenges רב's rule: the lamp is not holy, so why should using its light be forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this before שמואל, he said to me: Does the lamp have holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה reports that שמואל questioned the rule. שמואל argues that only holy things are forbidden for use, and the נר חנוכה is not holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל assumes that a ban on benefit only makes sense for something with real קדושה, like הקדש. Since the נר חנוכה has no such status, he sees no basis for the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it really? (introduces a challenging question)

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
he said to me:
Does the lamp have holiness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ban on counting money by the נר חנוכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ban on benefit requires holiness, and the lamp has none.

steps.title: רב יוסף pushes back: Is blood holy?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects שמואל's question by pointing to blood, which is not holy but still must be treated with respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף strongly objected to this: Does blood have holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks שמואל's question. He hints at a case where respect is required even without holiness, and the next step explains that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's challenge assumed that only holy things need special treatment. רב יוסף answers with a counterexample: the blood of a slaughtered חיה or bird is not holy, yet the halacha demands that it be treated respectfully. So holiness is not the only reason for such rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood (here, of a slaughtered חיה or bird)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objected to it:
Does blood have holiness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects שמואל's challenge to רב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption behind שמואל's question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל assumes that only holy things require respectful treatment, but blood is not holy and still requires it.

steps.title: Covering blood by hand, not by foot
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the blood must be covered by hand, not by foot, so that מצוות are not treated with contempt. The same reason applies to the נר חנוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'He shall spill… and cover': with what he spilled, he shall cover. He should not cover it with his foot, so that מצוות will not be disgraced in his eyes. Here too, so that מצוות will not be disgraced in his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא about כיסוי הדם to back up his point. He then applies its reason to the נר חנוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the hand did the slaughtering, the hand must do the covering. Using a foot would show disrespect for the מצוה. The concern is not holiness but בזיון מצוה, and the same concern forbids using the חנוכה light for trivial tasks like counting money.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
He shall spill and cover (ויקרא י״ז:י״ג)

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on counting money by the חנוכה light is not because the lamp is holy. It is to avoid treating a מצוה with contempt, just like covering blood by hand and not by foot.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'He shall spill [its blood] and cover [it]':
With that with which he spilled, he shall cover.
phrases.notes: He slaughtered with his hand, so he must cover with his hand.

phrases.english: He should not cover it with the foot,
so that מצוות will not be disgraced in his eyes.
Here too,
so that מצוות will not be disgraced in his eyes.
phrases.notes: Applied to the נר חנוכה: do not use its light for trivial purposes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source and reasoning behind רב יוסף's pushback.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule against using the light of the נר חנוכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on כיסוי הדם: cover with the hand, not the foot, so that מצוות are not treated with contempt.

steps.title: May one use נויי סוכה during the festival?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי is asked whether one may take and use the decorations of a סוכה during all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי יהושע בן לוי: May one take benefit from the decorations of a סוכה all seven days?
steps.whatsHappening: A related question is brought: can the decorations hanging in a סוכה be used, for example eaten, during סוכות? This sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the חנוכה light, נויי סוכה are tied to a מצוה. The question is whether that connection forbids personal benefit from them for the whole festival.

keyTerms.meaning: To take benefit from, to use
All seven days of the festival

phrases.aramaic: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: They asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
What is the law about using the decorations of a sukka
all seven days?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a parallel question about benefiting from objects connected to a מצוה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may use נויי סוכה during the festival.

steps.title: Answered from the נר חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers by citing the ban on counting money by the חנוכה light, which implies that נויי סוכה are forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: They already said it is forbidden to count money opposite a נר חנוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: He answers the סוכה question by comparing it to the חנוכה rule. Since one may not benefit from the חנוכה light, one may not benefit from נויי סוכה either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He treats רב's חנוכה rule as a general principle against using מצוה objects for personal benefit. He then applies that principle to the סוכה decorations.

phrases.english: He said to them:
They already said: it is forbidden to count money
opposite a Hanukkah light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the סוכה decorations.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is forbidden, by comparison to the ban on benefiting from the חנוכה light.

steps.title: רב יוסף: You are proving the known from the unknown
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects that the סוכה law is stated in a ברייתא while the חנוכה law is not, so the חנוכה rule cannot serve as the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Master of אברהם! He makes what was taught depend on what was not taught. סוכה was taught; חנוכה was not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף exclaims in surprise against רבי יהושע בן לוי's answer. The source should run the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on נויי סוכה appears explicitly in a ברייתא. The חנוכה rule is only an אמורא's statement. Using a less established rule to prove a better established one is backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of Abraham! (an exclamation of surprise)
He hangs what was taught on what was not taught

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Master of Abraham!
He makes what was taught depend on what was not taught.
Sukka was taught,
Hanukkah was not taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the method of רבי יהושע בן לוי's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's use of the חנוכה rule as the source for the סוכה law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סוכה law has a stronger source (a ברייתא), so it cannot depend on the weaker חנוכה statement.

steps.title: The ברייתא on נויי סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites the ברייתא: decorations hung in a proper סוכה may not be used until the festival ends, unless one made a condition beforehand.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If he roofed it properly, decorated it with colored hangings and decorated sheets, and hung in it nuts, peaches, almonds, pomegranates, grape clusters, wreaths of grain stalks, wines, oils, and flour, it is forbidden to use them until the end of the last יום טוב of the חג. And if he made a condition about them, everything follows his condition!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף quotes the ברייתא that explicitly forbids using סוכה decorations. This proves that the סוכה law is already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decorations take on a dedicated status for the whole festival and may not be taken for personal use. A condition made in advance allows using them, which shows that the ban comes from the decorations being set aside for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: He roofed it according to its halacha
The end of the last festival day

phrases.english: As it was taught: If he roofed it according to its halacha
and decorated it with colorful hangings
and with decorated sheets,
and hung in it nuts, peaches,
almonds and pomegranates,
and clusters of grapes
and wreaths of grain stalks,
wines, oils, and fine flour:
it is forbidden to use them

phrases.aramaic: עַד מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג.
phrases.english: until the end of the last festival day of the Chag.
And if he made a condition about them,
everything follows his condition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves רב יוסף's claim that the סוכה law is explicitly taught.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the סוכה law is already taught in a ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא forbidding use of סוכה decorations until after the festival, unless a condition was made.

steps.title: The source for them all is blood
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף concludes that the original source for all these rules is כיסוי הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: The father of them all is blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the proper source. It is neither חנוכה nor סוכה, but the law of covering blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The base principle of not treating מצוות with contempt comes from a פסוק, the covering of blood by hand. Both the חנוכה light rule and the סוכה decorations rule grow out of it. So the חנוכה rule is not the root, and the root is the תורה source from step 11.
steps.whatToRemember: All the laws against disrespecting מצוה objects (the חנוכה light, נויי סוכה) trace back to כיסוי הדם: cover the blood by hand, not by foot, so that מצוות are not treated with contempt.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
The father of them all is blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי יהושע בן לוי's proof with the true root source.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The root source for the ban on treating מצוה objects with contempt is כיסוי הדם, not the חנוכה light.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about lighting from one lamp to another
steps.stepSummary: רב forbids lighting one חנוכה lamp from another. שמואל permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב said, one may not light from one lamp to another lamp. שמואל said, one may light that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a dispute between רב and שמואל about lighting one חנוכה lamp from another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a person taking the flame of one חנוכה light to light another חנוכה light. רב says this is not allowed. שמואל says it is allowed. We are not yet told why רב forbids it. The גמרא explains that later.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated. This introduces a dispute between אמוראים.
From one lamp to another lamp

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav said
one may not light from lamp to lamp,
and Shmuel said: one may light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new dispute connected to the honor of the חנוכה light, which steps 8–11 discussed (steps 12–16 extended it to נויי סוכה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: lighting from נר to נר is forbidden. שמואל: it is permitted.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about moving ציצית from one garment to another
steps.stepSummary: רב forbids untying ציצית from one garment to put them on another. שמואל permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said, one may not untie ציצית from one garment to put them on another garment. שמואל said, one may untie them from one garment for another garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second dispute between רב and שמואל that has the same pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here one takes ציצית off an old garment to tie them onto a new garment. As before, רב is strict and שמואל is lenient. The parallel is that the case before also moved something from one מצוה object to another.

keyTerms.meaning: From one garment to another garment

phrases.english: Rav said: one may not untie ritual fringes
from garment to garment,
and Shmuel said: one may untie
from garment to garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel dispute between רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: moving ציצית between garments is forbidden. שמואל: it is permitted.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree whether the halacha follows רבי שמעון on dragging
steps.stepSummary: רב says the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון about dragging objects on שבת. שמואל says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said, the הלכה is not like רבי שמעון in the case of dragging. שמואל said, the הלכה is like רבי שמעון in the case of dragging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third dispute between רב and שמואל, this time about dragging furniture on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון allows dragging furniture on שבת even though it might make a groove in the ground, because the person does not intend to dig. רב does not rule like him, while שמואל does. The exact words of רבי שמעון are quoted two steps later.

keyTerms.meaning: Dragging an object along the ground

phrases.english: Rav said: the halakha is not
like Rabbi Shimon regarding dragging,
and Shmuel said: the halakha is
like Rabbi Shimon regarding dragging.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּגְרִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third dispute in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the הלכה is not like רבי שמעון on גרירה. שמואל: the הלכה is like רבי שמעון.

steps.title: אביי reports that his teacher followed שמואל in these three cases
steps.stepSummary: אביי says his teacher (מר, meaning רבה) normally followed רב, but in these three cases he followed שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: in all matters, the Master acted like רב, except for these three, where he acted like שמואל. He lit from lamp to lamp, untied ציצית from garment to garment, and held the הלכה is like רבי שמעון on dragging.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells us how his teacher actually ruled in these three disputes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, in ritual law, the rule is that רב is followed over שמואל. אביי reports that רבה made an exception here and followed שמואל in all three cases. This gives us the practical outcome: all three are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master. Here it means רבה, אביי's teacher.

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, רבה followed שמואל: lighting from נר to נר is allowed, moving ציצית is allowed, and the הלכה is like רבי שמעון on dragging.
steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us the practical ruling for all three disputes.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כֹּל מִילֵּי דְּמָר עָבֵיד כְּרַב
phrases.english: Abaye said: in all matters the Master acted according to Rav,
phrases.notes: מר refers to רבה, אביי's teacher.

phrases.english: except these three, where he acted according to Shmuel:
one may light from lamp to lamp,
and one may untie from garment to garment,
and the halakha is like Rabbi Shimon regarding dragging.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כֹּל מִילֵּי דְּמָר עָבֵיד כְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the practical ruling for the three disputes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In these three cases, practice follows שמואל.

steps.title: The baraita of רבי שמעון on dragging furniture
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון: a person may drag a bed, chair, or bench, as long as he does not intend to make a groove.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says, a person may drag a bed, a chair, or a bench, as long as he does not intend to make a groove.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source of רבי שמעון's opinion on dragging that was mentioned above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's principle is that an unintended result is not forbidden. Dragging furniture might dig a groove in the ground, which is a שבת violation. Since the person does not want to dig, it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A groove or furrow in the ground

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not allow digging a groove. He allows dragging even if a groove might form by accident, as long as the person does not intend it.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
a person may drag a bed, chair, and bench —
as long as he does not intend to make a furrow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text for the גרירה ruling.
steps.raayaObject: What רבי שמעון's position on גרירה is

steps.title: A scholar explains that רב's reason is disrespect to the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: A scholar sitting before רב אדא בר אהבה says רב forbade lighting from נר to נר because it is ביזוי מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages sat before רב אדא בר אהבה, and he sat and said: רב's reason is because of disrespect to the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks why רב forbade lighting from lamp to lamp. A scholar suggests the first reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that taking the flame of the חנוכה light for another use, such as lighting a plain stick to carry the flame, treats the מצוה as cheap. This reason focuses on the dignity of the מצוה, not on any holiness of the lamp.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain one of the scholars

phrases.english: One of the Sages sat
before Rav Adda bar Ahava
and he sat and said:
Rav's reason is due to contempt for the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first dispute (step 17) to explain רב's reasoning.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה rejects that and says the reason is weakening the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה tells his students not to listen. רב's reason is that it weakens the מצוה (אכחושי מצוה).
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Do not listen to him. רב's reason is because he weakens the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה rejects the scholar's explanation and gives a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weakening the מצוה means that taking a flame from the חנוכה lamp slightly uses up its oil or wick, which were set aside for the מצוה. This reason is about physically reducing the מצוה object, not about disrespect.

phrases.english: He said to them: do not listen to him,
Rav's reason is because
he weakens the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 22's reason and replaces it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reason given for רב, not רב's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The issue is diminishing the מצוה object, not disrespect.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the two reasons differ in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to different rulings. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons explain why רב forbids lighting. The גמרא wants a case where one reason forbids and the other permits.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between steps 22 and 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where ביזוי מצוה and אכחושי מצוה give different rulings

steps.title: The difference is lighting directly from lamp to lamp
steps.stepSummary: If one lights directly from one חנוכה lamp to another, ביזוי מצוה permits it, but אכחושי מצוה forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference when he lights directly from lamp to lamp. The one who says the reason is disrespect: from lamp to lamp he may light. The one who says the reason is weakening the מצוה: even from lamp to lamp it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by giving the case where the two reasons split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lighting through a plain stick means the light is used for something that is not a מצוה, so both reasons forbid it. Lighting one חנוכה lamp directly from another is not disrespectful, because the second lamp is also a מצוה. However, it still uses up some of the first lamp's oil and wick, so it counts as weakening the מצוה.
steps.whatToRemember: ביזוי מצוה permits lighting directly from one חנוכה lamp to another. אכחושי מצוה forbids even that.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the two lighting methods. Lighting through a plain stick is forbidden by both reasons. Only direct lighting from one חנוכה lamp to another is where they disagree.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he lights directly from lamp to lamp:
the one who said it is due to contempt for the מצוה —
from lamp to lamp he may light.
The one who said it is due to weakening the מצוה —
even from lamp to lamp it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּקָא מַדְלֵיק מִשְּׁרָגָא לִשְׁרָגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Direct lighting from one חנוכה lamp to another is permitted according to ביזוי מצוה and forbidden according to אכחושי מצוה.
